channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajik Parliament Approves Investment Deals Linked to President's Relatives
item.description: Tajikistan's lower house of parliament approved five investment agreements with private companies on November 23. Two of these companies, a telecom firm and a metallurgical plant, are reportedly linked to relatives of President Emomali Rahmon. The agreements aim to develop the telecommunications sector and establish cement production facilities. International financial institutions have previously criticized Tajikistan for opaque benefit allocations to certain companies.

item.title: Hundreds of Healthcare Workers in Akmola Region Denied Social Insurance Contributions
item.description: Prosecutors in the Sandyktau district of Kazakhstan's Akmola region have uncovered violations affecting over 338 healthcare workers. These workers did not receive mandatory social health insurance contributions for two months, potentially jeopardizing their insurance status. The employer has since paid over 4 million tenge in overdue contributions following prosecutorial intervention.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans pilot project to hire border guards with foreign language skills
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Border Service plans to launch a pilot project to select officers proficient in English and other foreign languages for border crossing points. Candidates will be chosen based on exams, with requirements including language proficiency and a minimum height of 170 cm. The project is expected to facilitate communication with foreign visitors and accommodate an anticipated threefold increase in tourist flow next year.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Installment Service Providers Must Register with Central Bank from 2027
item.description: From January 1, 2027, providers of goods and services on installment in Uzbekistan will be required to register with the Central Bank. This applies to companies with monthly turnovers exceeding 500 million soums, where at least half comes from installment payments. Banks and MFIs will be registered upon notification.

item.title: President Dismisses Yerassyl Nagaspayev as Minister of Industry and Construction
item.description: Kazakhstan's Head of State, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, has dismissed Yerassyl Nagaspayev from his position as Minister of Industry and Construction. The Akorda's press service reported the dismissal, stating that the decree was signed by the Head of State. No further details were provided.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prime Minister Mandates Aitu for Official Communications
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed government bodies to accelerate the development and widespread adoption of the Aitu national digital ecosystem for daily work. He emphasized that official information must be transmitted exclusively through this national messenger, aiming to create a comprehensive digital model.

item.title: CIS Countries to Develop Strategy for Cooperation in School Nutrition
item.description: CIS member states will develop a cooperation strategy for school nutrition. This decision was made at a meeting of the Council for Educational Cooperation in Dushanbe. The document will assess the state and formation of institutions for developing the material and technical base of student catering, as well as the infrastructure for school nutrition.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Minister of Industry and Construction Dismissed by President
item.description: President has dismissed Yersaiyn Nagaspayev from his post as Minister of Industry and Construction. Nagaspayev had led the ministry since February 28, 2025, retaining his position after a September 2026 reappointment. The dismissal follows President's earlier statement regarding serious concerns about the quality of some new residential buildings.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Family Switches to Heat Pump, Reduces Winter Heating Costs
item.description: A family in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region has replaced coal heating with a heat pump, financed by a state loan. Previously spending 50-60,000 soms on coal annually, the family's electricity bill for October was around 1,000 soms for their 150 sq meter home.

item.title: Armenia Launches 'Trump Route' Project Amidst Iranian Concerns
item.description: Armenia has officially launched the 'Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity' project, aiming to expand transit and economic links in the South Caucasus. Iran expressed concerns over potential foreign military presence near its borders and the project's impact on its transit revenues.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Orders Systematic Improvement of Mobile Network Coverage
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed the Ministry of Digital Development to systematically identify and address areas with unstable mobile communication. Citizens continue to report poor signal quality in populated areas and along roads. The ministry, along with local authorities and operators, must update a map of 'dead zones' and set deadlines for their resolution within a month.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Update National Emblem and Awards to Reflect New Latin Alphabet
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering changes to its national emblem and awards to align with the updated Latin-based alphabet. The name 'Oʻzbekiston' on the emblem may be changed to 'Özbekiston'. Government bodies are expected to submit proposals for these changes by June 2027, as part of a broader initiative to implement the new alphabet across all spheres of public life.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Digitize State Language Certificates via 'Tunduk' App
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is proposing to issue digital certificates for state language proficiency through the 'Tunduk' mobile application. A draft resolution suggests amending the existing 'KyrgyzTest' system to allow electronic certificates, with paper options available upon request. This change aims to formalize the current practice, which began in September 2026.

item.title: Smart Solar-Powered Water Meters Installed in Karakalpakstan for Irrigation Control
item.description: Smart, solar-powered water metering systems have been installed on 13 farms in the Amudarya district of Karakalpakstan to control water flow in irrigation canals. These devices measure and regulate water volume, crucial for downstream farms. The project also includes training farmers on modern water management technologies and water user rights.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Limiting Beef Exports to Control Domestic Prices
item.description: The Kazakh government is exploring measures to restrict beef and lamb exports to ensure domestic supply and stabilize prices. This comes amid rising meat costs, with poultry and processed meats seeing significant increases. Agricultural fairs will also be expanded to allow direct purchasing from producers.

item.title: Over 32 Million People Crossed Kyrgyz-Uzbek Border in 10 Months
item.description: More than 32 million people and over 3 million vehicles traversed the Kyrgyz-Uzbek border in the first 10 months of 2026. Amendments to a 2004 agreement aim to upgrade border crossing points, potentially changing their status to multilateral and enabling 24/7 operation to ease congestion and boost trade.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Favors Subsidies Over Tax Cuts for Continuous Fuel Supply
item.description: Almambet Shykmyamatov, head of the State Tax Service, stated that maintaining a subsidy mechanism for fuel imports is the most appropriate measure to ensure a continuous supply of fuel in Kyrgyzstan. He believes subsidies compensate for additional costs for suppliers, creating equal conditions, and are preferable to tax changes which could cause administrative difficulties.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Disrupts 19 Drug Trafficking Routes, Seizes Over a Ton of Narcotics
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has dismantled five clandestine drug laboratories and blocked 19 drug supply channels between August and October. Authorities seized over 1.3 tons of narcotics, including opium, hashish, marijuana, and synthetic drugs, arresting 45 individuals, including five foreigners.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Mandating Fiber Optic Internet in New Apartments
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a new construction standard requiring new homes to be equipped with fiber optic internet cables to each apartment and space for 4G/5G base stations. The proposal, put forth by Kazakhtelecom's chairman, aims to treat internet connectivity as a basic utility like electricity or water, with stricter penalties for cable damage.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seizes Over 1.3 Tons of Drugs in Three Months
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee reported seizing over 1.3 tons of drugs during anti-narcotics operations from August to October 2026. The operations disrupted 8 international and 11 regional drug trafficking channels, shut down 5 clandestine laboratories, and involved joint efforts with foreign authorities. 40 citizens and 5 foreigners were detained.

item.title: Qatar Warns of New Escalation Risk Between US and Iran, Pushes for Talks
item.description: Qatar's Prime Minister warned that the Middle East cannot withstand another escalation between the US and Iran, emphasizing Doha's ongoing efforts to mediate renewed negotiations. The statement followed a meeting with the US Secretary of State, during which the eighth US-Qatar Strategic Dialogue was launched. The US expressed gratitude for Qatar's mediation efforts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank Eases Bank Liquidity Management Rules
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has updated rules for calculating the instant liquidity ratio for commercial banks. Banks can now include government securities with up to 180 days until maturity, an increase from the previous seven days. These changes aim to enhance banks' ability to manage short-term financial obligations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kazakhtelecom Network Damaged 459 Times in 2026
item.description: Kazakhtelecom's networks were damaged 459 times by external organizations in the first 10 months of 2026, resulting in 80 days of downtime. One incident in the Zhetysu region affected over 15,000 subscribers and caused internet traffic reductions in Semey and Pavlodar.

item.title: Over 29,000 Students Enrolled in Kyrgyz Vocational Lyceums, Ministry Reports
item.description: Currently, 29,474 individuals are studying in vocational lyceums across Kyrgyzstan, with 96.9% funded by the national budget, according to the Deputy Minister of Education. In 2026, 18,431 new students were admitted. High-demand professions include chefs, mechanics, welders, IT specialists, and seamstresses.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks Seventh Globally for Affordable Mobile Internet
item.description: Kazakhstan ranks seventh out of 55 countries for mobile internet affordability, with an average monthly cost of around $10, nearly three times lower than the global average of $27. The country also entered the UN's top tier for digital government development. Officials aim to balance affordable tariffs with investment attractiveness.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Questions Digital Vice Premier on ChatGPT and Aitu Usage
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev raised questions regarding the usage of ChatGPT and Aitu following a report by the digital vice-premier. The president inquired about the number of Kazakh citizens utilizing these platforms. Several videos from the meeting have been released.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Legal Status for Internet as Infrastructure Service
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Digital Development, Bagdat Mussin, proposed legally recognizing the internet as an infrastructure service. This follows recent incidents where damaged cables disrupted service for thousands. He also suggested strengthening penalties for damaging communication lines, citing 459 such incidents this year alone.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Customs Seizes Over 15 Kilograms of Undeclared Jewelry
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's customs officials discovered over 15 kilograms of undeclared jewelry in two shipments of household goods arriving from the UAE and China. The silver items, including rings, earrings, and chains, were found during inspections at the 'ZhD Vokzal' customs post. The estimated state damage was compensated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Chief Explains Why Personal Accounts Aren't Blocked for QR Payments
item.description: Almambet Shykymatov, head of Kyrgyzstan's State Tax Service, stated they are not currently blocking personal bank accounts used for QR code payments by businesses. He prefers dialogue and education over strict measures, acknowledging that forced blocking could cause public discontent. The service aims to foster tax culture.

item.title: Central Asian Migrants Increasingly Opt for Europe Over Russia for Work
item.description: Labor migrants from Central Asia are increasingly viewing European countries as an alternative to Russia. Stricter Russian migration laws, increased deportations, and a weaker ruble are contributing factors. Many seek more stable work and higher incomes in EU nations like Poland and Germany.

item.title: Kazakhstan Telecom Seeks Harsher Penalties for Communication Line Damage
item.description: Kazakhstan's 'Kazakhtelecom' proposes stricter penalties for damaging communication lines. The company reported 459 instances of network damage by third parties in 10 months, causing 80 days of downtime. A recent incident affected over 15,000 subscribers and disrupted services across multiple regions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's State Security Committee Admits Flaws in Asset Recovery Efforts
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (SCNS) acknowledged shortcomings in its fight against organized crime and corruption, particularly in recovering state assets. SCNS head Maksat Asanaliev stated that while legal procedures were followed, some irregularities occurred during the process of returning seized property.

item.title: Tajikistan to Develop Digital System for Collecting Child Abuse Data by 2028
item.description: Tajikistan plans to develop a unified digital system for collecting and analyzing data on child abuse by the end of 2028. The country also aims to fully implement its National Program for Child Rights Protection Reform by 2030. Discussions at a global conference focused on child protection, online safety, and inter-agency cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh Court Overturns Early Release of Former Governor Convicted of Corruption
item.description: The Almaty Regional Court on November 23 overturned the early release of Karim Kokrekbaev, former governor of Zhambyl region and ex-ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, who was sentenced to 12 years for bribery. The court found the release, granted due to severe illness, to be unfounded.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Develop AI Models for Film Production Using National Heritage Data
item.description: Uzbekistan's national film company, O'zbekfilm, will integrate artificial intelligence into filmmaking by 2028. A database of the country's history, culture, and visual heritage will be compiled for AI models. A new O'zbekfilm AI Lab will train specialists and implement AI solutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sees Sharp Rise in Retail Fuel Prices Over One Week
item.description: Retail prices for automotive fuel in Uzbekistan increased significantly between November 11 and 18. AI-91 gasoline rose by 758 soms per liter in some regions, AI-92 by 648 soms, propane by 368 soms, and methane by 451 soms. Average prices also saw notable increases.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Public Meetings with President Reveal Justice System Inefficiencies
item.description: Public meetings held by Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov across the country transformed into pleas for justice, highlighting the ineffectiveness of existing legal mechanisms. Citizens perceive the president as the sole guarantor of justice, with common complaints focusing on law enforcement and judicial bodies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Builds Internet Hyper-Highway from Khorgos to Aktau
item.description: Kazakhstan is constructing a 'West-East' internet hyper-highway, with 87% of the route already laid. The project aims to boost internet traffic transit through the country and is expected to be completed next year. This initiative, along with the Trans-Caspian fiber-optic line, will enhance data transmission capabilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Establish Special Posts for Safe Refilling of Household Gas Cylinders
item.description: Uzbekistan's 'Hududgaztaminot' company is proposing the establishment of special posts at gas filling stations for the safe refilling of household gas cylinders. This initiative aims to create additional opportunities for the public to refill their domestic gas cylinders securely. Relevant organizations have received proposals for this purpose.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Simplifying Telecom Equipment Installation on Residential Buildings
item.description: Kazakhstan's telecom operators face difficulties installing base stations on residential buildings due to resident objections, leading to the annual dismantling of about 150 stations. The company "Kcell" requested government assistance to simplify the installation procedure, citing resident "radio-phobia" as a primary obstacle.
